title: Diagonal orientation of a vector bundle
statement:
Work in the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $n\geq1$, so $\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\pi:V\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$ with zero section [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. No separatedness of $S$ over $k$ is assumed. Use the small pro-etale categories, constructible exceptional inverse image and specified Tate twists of these conventions.

Let $\vartheta_\pi:\omega_\pi=R\pi^!\Lambda_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_V(d)[2d]$ be the diagonal orientation of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]: on separated affine target charts it is the composite of diagonal base change, the normalized deformation-to-the-normal-bundle comparison and vector-bundle purity, and these chart maps are glued as in that construction. Let $t_\pi:R\pi_!\Lambda_V(d)[2d]\to\Lambda_S$ be integration along the fibres [def-amb-vector-integration], realized with the specified pro-etale twists and compact supports by [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. Let $P_\pi:\Lambda_V(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi^!\Lambda_S$ be its exceptional adjoint transpose, the vector-bundle purity isomorphism whose inverse is specified in [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. Then
$$\vartheta_\pi=P_\pi^{-1}.$$
Thus the diagonal orientation equals the vector-bundle orientation, with the same integration normalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-vector-bundle-finite-type-frames] to obtain affine finite-type trivializing opens $U_i$ and $V_i=\pi^{-1}U_i\cong\mathbf A^d_{U_i}$; $\pi$ is separated finite type and smooth of dimension $d$. All diagonal/DNC model applications below take place on these separated affine charts.

source.place: Reassembly of returned proof Steps 1; see report argument-preservation map

proof.text: On a frame put $p:V_i\to U_i$ and $\vartheta_i=\beta_i\delta_i\alpha_i^{-1}$. By [lem-pur-vector-bundle-frame-orientation-restriction] this is the restriction of $\vartheta_\pi$, and the restriction of $P_\pi$ is the actual integration adjunct $P_p$, with the same exceptional and Tate identifications. These identifications agree on affine refinements of chart overlaps.

source.place: Reassembly of returned proof Steps 2; see report argument-preservation map

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] to $p$ at $K=\Lambda_{U_i}$, a bounded constructible coefficient unit of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. It gives $\gamma_{p,\Lambda}=\Gamma_{p,\Lambda}$. By [lem-pur-affine-ordered-integration-transposes], the ordered counit recursion, starting with the identity at rank zero, identifies $\Gamma_{p,\Lambda}=P_p$ for the actual integration and its specified site realization.

source.place: Reassembly of returned proof Steps 3; see report argument-preservation map

proof.text: By [lem-pur-dualizing-unit-composite], $\theta_{p,\Lambda}$ is the canonical unit identification. Substituting this into [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], the twist reassociation and unitors cancel and give $\gamma_{p,\Lambda}=\vartheta_i^{-1}$. Hence $\vartheta_i=P_p^{-1}$. Step 2 now gives equality of the restrictions of $\vartheta_\pi$ and $P_\pi^{-1}$ on every $V_i$.

source.place: Reassembly of returned proof Steps 4; see report argument-preservation map

proof.text: Set $L=\Lambda_V(d)$ and $h=\vartheta_\pi P_\pi\in\operatorname{Aut}(L[2d])$. The finite Tate line is locally free of rank one in degree zero by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3); its $d$-fold tensor power is therefore also a degree-zero sheaf (locally it is the coefficient unit). Remove the common shift. By [lem-pur-degree-zero-derived-map-gluing], equality of endomorphisms of $L[0]$ can be checked on the Zariski cover $\{V_i\}$. Step 4 gives identity on every restriction, so $h[-2d]=1$ and $h=1$. Cancel $P_\pi$ to obtain $\vartheta_\pi=P_\pi^{-1}$. The same argument includes empty bases and rank zero, without reducedness or connectedness.
